name: Banana + Soaked Almonds
description: Light carb + healthy fats for steady energy.

steps: Drain soaked almonds; peel if preferred.
Slice banana into a bowl.
Add almonds and a pinch of cinnamon.
Eat 30–45 minutes before training with water.

nutritionNotes: Medium banana (~118g): ~105 kcal, 1.3g protein, 27g carbs (USDA).
8–10 almonds (~12g): ~70 kcal, ~2.5g protein, ~6g fat.
Combined estimate ~185 kcal · ~4–5g protein.

name: Poha with Peanuts
description: Classic light Indian breakfast with carbs and crunch.
portion: 1 medium bowl (~200g) poha with 1 tbsp peanuts

steps: Rinse poha and drain; it should soften but not turn mushy.
Heat oil; temper mustard, curry leaves, peanuts.
Sauté onion till translucent; add turmeric and salt.
Fold in poha, cover 1–2 minutes, finish with lemon and coriander.
Serve one medium bowl 45–60 min before workout.

nutritionNotes: Portion ~200g cooked poha + 1 tbsp (~10g) peanuts.
Cooked poha ~136 kcal & ~2.7g protein / 100g (common Indian nutrition tables); peanuts ~57 kcal & ~2.6g protein / 10g.
Estimate ~315 kcal · 8g protein for this bowl (oil/veg vary ±10%).

name: Moong Dal Chilla
description: Protein-rich savory pancake, easy to digest.

ingredients: 1 cup moong dal (soaked 2–3 hrs) or 3/4 cup moong flour
steps: Blend soaked dal with chilli, ginger, salt to a pourable batter (or mix flour with water).
Stir in chopped veggies if using.
Spread thin pancakes on a hot non-stick pan; cook both sides with light oil.
Make 2 medium chillas; serve with chutney about 60 min before training.

name: Idli with Sambar
description: Light fermented carbs with lentil protein.

steps: Warm idlis by steaming or microwave briefly with a damp cloth.
Heat sambar until simmering; adjust salt and tempering if needed.
Serve 3 idlis with a small bowl of sambar.
Eat 45–60 minutes before your session.

name: Rava Upma
description: Warm semolina bowl with veggies.

steps: Dry-roast rava until aromatic; set aside.
Temper mustard, chilli, curry leaves; sauté onion and veggies.
Add water and salt; bring to a boil.
Lower heat, stir in rava, cover 2–3 minutes until fluffy.
Serve one medium bowl 45–60 min pre-workout.

name: Whole Wheat Toast + Peanut Butter
description: Quick carb-protein combo.

name: Curd Rice (light bowl)
description: Cooling carbs with probiotics.

steps: Mash rice lightly and mix with whisked curd and salt until creamy.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, chilli, and ginger in ½ tsp oil.
Pour tempering over curd rice and stir.
Eat a small bowl 60–75 min before training; keep it light.

name: Fruit Bowl + Curd
description: Hydrating carbs with dairy protein.

ingredients: 1 cup chopped seasonal fruit (banana, papaya, or apple)
steps: Whisk curd until smooth.
Fold in chopped fruit and optional honey.
Add cardamom if you like.
Eat 30–45 min before training with a glass of water.

name: Masala Oats
description: Savory oats with veggies for sustained energy.
nutritionNotes: ~50g dry rolled oats: ~190 kcal, ~6.5g protein, ~34g carbs (USDA oats).
Masala prep with ~1 tsp oil + veg: +~70–80 kcal; protein ~9–10g bowl.

name: Egg Bhurji on Toast
description: Fast protein with carbs for morning sessions.

name: Banana + Plant Protein Smoothie
description: Easy liquid calories if solid food feels heavy.

name: Plain Dosa + Chutney
description: Light fermented rice-lentil crepe.

name: Paneer Bhurji + Roti
description: High-protein North Indian recovery meal.

name: Sprouts Chaat + Curd
description: Protein-packed chaat with cooling curd.

steps: Steam or lightly sauté sprouts 3–4 min if raw digestion bothers you.
Toss with onion, tomato, lemon, chaat masala, and salt.
Serve with a side of thick curd.
Eat within 45 minutes after training for protein + carbs.

name: Whey/Plant Protein + Banana Smoothie
description: Fast recovery shake for supplement users.
nutritionNotes: Typical whey scoop (~30g powder): ~110–120 kcal, ~24g protein (label average).
Medium banana: ~105 kcal, 1.3g protein (USDA). Water mix keeps fat low.

name: Rajma Chawal
description: Hearty post leg-day meal with complete carbs + protein.
nutritionNotes: Portion: ~150g cooked rajma (with light gravy) + ~180g cooked rice.
Cooked kidney beans ~127 kcal & ~8.7g protein / 100g; cooked rice ~130 kcal & ~2.7g protein / 100g (USDA-style).
With modest oil in gravy: ~455 kcal · ~17–18g protein (home recipes often 420–480 kcal).

name: Egg Curry + Rice
description: Eggetarian classic with solid protein.

name: Chicken Breast + Jeera Rice
description: Lean non-veg recovery plate.

name: Dal Tadka + Roti + Salad
description: Everyday vegetarian recovery combo.

name: Tofu Bhurji + Millet Roti
description: Vegan high-protein alternative to paneer.

name: Grilled Fish + Lemon Rice
description: Omega-rich South-leaning recovery meal.

name: Chana Masala + Brown Rice
description: Fiber-rich plant protein bowl.
portion: 1 katori chana masala + 1 bowl brown rice

name: Stuffed Paneer Paratha + Dahi
description: Heartier North Indian recovery option.

ingredients: 1 tsp ghee or oil for roasting
steps: Stuff dough with spiced paneer and seal edges.
Roll gently and roast on a tawa with light ghee until golden.
Serve hot with a bowl of dahi.
Best as a fuller meal ~90 min after a hard session.

name: Sambar Rice + Beans Poriyal
description: South Indian balanced recovery plate.
portion: 1 plate sambar rice + 1 cup beans poriyal

name: Hung Curd Bowl + Fruits + Seeds
description: High-protein snackable recovery bowl.
portion: 200g hung curd + 1 cup fruit + 1 tsp seeds

ingredients: 200g hung curd or thick Greek-style yogurt
steps: Hang curd in a muslin for 20–30 min if starting from regular dahi (or use thick yogurt).
Spoon into a bowl and top with fruit.
Sprinkle seeds (and nuts if no allergy).
Eat within 30–45 min post-workout as a high-protein snack.

name: Soya Chunk Curry + Roti
description: Budget-friendly high-protein veg meal.
portion: 1 katori soya curry (~80g dry soya cooked) + 2 rotis

name: Masala Omelette + Multigrain Bread
description: Quick eggetarian recovery.

name: Moong Dal Khichdi + Ghee
description: Gentle on stomach after tough sessions.
portion: 1 large bowl moong khichdi (~250g) + 1 tsp ghee

name: Spiced Chaas (Buttermilk)
description: Light yogurt drink that hydrates without heaviness.

ingredients: Pinch of roasted cumin powder + salt
steps: Whisk curd until lump-free.
Add water, cumin, salt; froth well.
Add chopped mint if using.
Sip cool — ideal when a full meal feels too heavy.

name: Curd Parfait with Seeds
description: Layered yogurt snack with carbs and crunch.

steps: Layer curd and fruit in a glass.
Top with seeds or a spoon of granola.
Drizzle honey only if you need extra carbs.
Eat calmly 45–60 min before lifting.

name: Mishti-Style Curd Recovery Bowl
description: Slightly sweet set curd with fruit for glycogen refill.

ingredients: 150g thick sweet curd (or plain curd + 1 tsp jaggery)
steps: If using plain curd, stir in grated jaggery until dissolved.
Top with sliced fruit and cardamom.
Keep portions modest — treat as recovery dessert, not a feast.
Pair with water; add a protein scoop only if your coach plan allows.

name: Vegetable Raita + Millet Khichu Bite
description: Cooling yogurt raita with a small millet carb side.
portion: 1 bowl veg raita + 1 small millet pancake/khichu

ingredients: 1 small millet flatbread or leftover bajra roti
steps: Mix veggies into curd with cumin and salt.
Warm millet side lightly if cold.
Eat raita with the millet bite for carbs + probiotics.
Great after sweaty sessions when appetite is low.

name: Whey Protein Water Shake
description: Light pre-lift shake — fast protein without a heavy meal.

ingredients: 1 scoop whey protein (unflavoured or low sugar)
steps: Add whey to a shaker with water.
Shake hard 15–20 seconds until smooth.
Sip 20–40 min before training if a solid meal feels heavy.

name: Plant Protein + Banana Shake
description: Dairy-free shake with a little fruit carb for energy.
portion: 1 scoop plant protein + ½ banana in water

steps: Blend or shake powder with water.
Add banana and blend until smooth.
Drink 30–45 min pre-session.

name: Whey + Oats Recovery Shake
description: Protein plus slow carbs for post-lift glycogen refill.
portion: 1 scoop whey + 30g oats blended in water/milk

steps: Blend oats briefly with liquid.
Add whey and blend until smooth (don’t over-foam).
Drink within 30 minutes post-workout.

name: Zero-Sugar Protein Mug Cake (No Maida)
description: Microwave cake using protein powder + oat/almond flour — no maida, no added sugar.

ingredients: 2 tbsp oat flour or almond flour (no maida)
1 egg or 60ml egg white / plant yogurt for vegan swap
Stevia or erythritol to taste (zero sugar)
Splash of water or unsweetened milk to batter
steps: Mix dry ingredients in a microwave-safe mug.
Stir in egg (or yogurt) and liquid to a thick batter — no refined flour, no sugar.
Microwave 60–90 seconds until just set (don’t overcook).
Cool a minute; eat as a post-workout treat.

name: Protein Skillet Pancake Cake (No Maida)
description: Pan “cake” stack from protein powder and oats — zero added sugar, no maida.

ingredients: Non-stick spray or ½ tsp oil
steps: Whisk protein, oat flour, egg, and water into a pourable batter.
Cook on a non-stick pan over medium heat like mini pancakes.
Stack two; no sugar syrup — cinnamon or berries if needed.
Eat warm after training.

name: Dates + Soaked Almonds
description: Quick natural carbs from khajoor with a little fat for steady pre-gym energy.

ingredients: 3–4 Medjool or soft Indian dates (khajoor), pitted
steps: Pit the dates if needed.
Pair with drained soaked almonds.
Eat with water 20–40 minutes before training.

nutritionNotes: 3 Medjool-class dates (~24g edible): ~66 kcal, ~0.5g protein, ~18g carbs each → ~200 kcal carbs-heavy.
Adjusted for 3–4 smaller Indian dates + 6–8 almonds (~12g): ~230 kcal · ~4–5g protein.

name: Dates + Banana
description: Double fruit carbs for longer or higher-intensity sessions.

steps: Slice banana and chop dates.
Eat together; sip water.
Best when you need fast fuel without dairy.

nutritionNotes: 2–3 dates + ½–1 banana: stacked fruit carbs for training fuel (USDA banana + date estimates).

name: Peanut Butter Stuffed Dates
description: Sticky-sweet dates with a spoon of clean peanut butter for satiety.
portion: 3 dates stuffed with 1 tsp peanut butter each

ingredients: 1 tbsp natural peanut butter (no sugar / no hydrogenated oil)
steps: Split dates and fill with peanut butter.
Eat slowly with water.
Allow ~45–60 min if your stomach is sensitive to fat pre-lift.

nutritionNotes: 3 dates + 1 tbsp natural peanut butter (~16g): PB ~94 kcal, ~4g protein, ~8g fat (USDA).

name: Dates + Thick Curd
description: Natural sugar from khajoor plus probiotic protein from dahi.

steps: Chop dates and fold into cold curd.
Add cardamom if you like.
Eat soon after training for carbs + protein.

nutritionNotes: 150–200g plain curd (~60–70 kcal/100g, ~3.5–4g protein/100g Indian dahi) + 3–4 dates.

name: Warm Milk with Dates
description: Classic recovery glass — milk protein with date carbs.
portion: 250ml milk + 3–4 soaked dates blended or mashed

steps: Soak dates 5 minutes in warm milk if hard.
Mash or blend until smooth.
Drink warm; add cinnamon if desired.

nutritionNotes: 250ml toned milk ~130–140 kcal, ~8g protein + 3–4 dates.

name: Whey + Dates Shake
description: Protein shake sweetened only with dates — no added sugar.

steps: Blend dates with liquid until smooth.
Add whey and blend briefly.
Drink immediately after training.

nutritionNotes: 1 scoop whey (~24g protein) + 2–3 dates for carbs instead of sugar.

name: Ragi Malt / Ambali
description: Finger-millet porridge for steady pre-gym carbs and mineral support.

ingredients: Optional: ½ tsp jaggery or 1 date, mashed
steps: Whisk ragi flour into cold water to avoid lumps.
Cook on low heat 6–8 min until thick and smooth.
Cool slightly; eat 45–60 min pre-session with water.

nutritionNotes: Dry ragi (ICMR–NIN/IIMR): ~336 kcal, 7.3g protein / 100g.
40g flour cooked as porridge ≈ 134 kcal + water; with optional date ~155 kcal · ~3g protein.

name: Ragi Dosa + Chutney
description: Crisp south-Indian ragi dosa for portable pre-workout carbs.
portion: 2 thin ragi dosas + 2 tbsp coconut/tomato chutney

steps: Mix flours with water into pourable batter; rest 10 min.
Spread thin on hot tawa; cook both sides.
Serve with light chutney; allow ~1 hr before heavy lifts if oily.

nutritionNotes: ~60g ragi flour (~200 kcal, ~4.4g protein) + little rice flour/oil + chutney.

name: Ragi Mudde + Sambar
description: Karnataka classic — millet ball with lentil sambar for recovery carbs + amino acids.
portion: 1 medium ragi mudde + 1 bowl vegetable sambar

steps: Cook ragi flour into a stiff ball (mudde) with salted water.
Serve hot with protein-rich sambar.
Eat soon after training for glycogen + plant protein.

nutritionNotes: Ragi mudde from ~65g flour + bowl sambar (dal protein). Ragi dry: 7.3g protein/100g (IIMR).
Dal pairing improves lysine (IIMR millet guidance).

name: Ragi Porridge + Curd
description: Warm ragi carbs with probiotic curd protein for easier post-lift digestion.

ingredients: 35g ragi flour cooked as soft porridge
steps: Cook smooth ragi porridge; cool to warm.
Swirl in curd or serve on the side.
Eat within 45 minutes post-session.

nutritionNotes: 35g ragi flour porridge + 100–120g curd for recovery protein.

name: Palak + Paneer Mini Wrap
description: Light spinach and paneer for iron/folate plus pre-lift protein.

ingredients: 1 small whole-wheat roti or millet roti
steps: Quick-sauté spinach with garlic; squeeze lemon (vitamin C aids non-heme iron).
Warm paneer cubes; wrap with roti.
Eat ~1 hr before training.

nutritionNotes: Cooked spinach (USDA): ~23 kcal, 3g protein, 3.6mg iron / 100g.
Paneer ~18–20g protein / 60g; roti adds carbs.

name: Spinach Egg Omelette
description: Fast protein omelette loaded with wilted spinach.

steps: Wilt spinach in pan; pour beaten eggs over.
Cook through; fold and plate.
Great when carbs are coming from a separate fruit side.

nutritionNotes: 2 large eggs ~140 kcal, 12g protein (USDA) + wilted spinach cup + 1 tsp oil.

name: Palak Dal
description: Spinach simmered with dal — iron + plant protein recovery bowl.
portion: 1 generous bowl palak dal + optional 1 small roti/rice scoop

steps: Temper spices; add tomato and spinach until wilted.
Stir into cooked dal; simmer 5 min.
Finish with lemon for iron absorption support.

nutritionNotes: Cooked dal + spinach; spinach adds folate/iron (USDA cooked spinach).

name: Spinach Tofu Stir-Fry
description: Vegan recovery plate with tofu protein and spinach micros.

steps: Pan-sear tofu cubes.
Add spinach until just wilted; season lightly.
Serve hot; add rice/ragi if you need more carbs.

nutritionNotes: Firm tofu ~150g ~170–190 kcal, ~18–20g protein; spinach micros from USDA.

name: Fresh Papaya Bowl
description: Light tropical carbs — vitamin C rich and easy on the stomach.

ingredients: Pinch of chaat masala or lime (optional)
steps: Cube papaya.
Add lime/chaat if desired.
Eat as a light pre-fuel.

nutritionNotes: Papaya ~43 kcal / 100g (USDA); ~250g bowl ≈ 110 kcal, high vitamin C.

name: Apple + Almond Butter
description: Fibre-rich apple carbs with a little nut butter for staying power.

steps: Slice apple.
Dip or spread almond butter.
Hydrate with water.

nutritionNotes: Medium apple ~95 kcal, 0.5g protein (USDA) + 1 tbsp almond butter ~98 kcal, ~3.4g protein.

name: Anar + Curd Cup
description: Antioxidant-rich pomegranate arils over protein curd.

steps: Spoon curd into a bowl.
Top with arils.
Eat chilled.

nutritionNotes: 150g curd + ½ cup arils (~87g, ~70 kcal). Curd protein ~5–6g / 150g.

name: Berry Curd Bowl
description: Berries for polyphenols with dairy protein for recovery.

steps: Top curd with berries.
No added sugar needed.
Eat soon after training.

nutritionNotes: 150–180g curd + ¾ cup berries (~50–60 kcal fruit).

name: Banana Peanut Butter Toast
description: Classic recovery toast — potassium carbs plus nut protein/fats.
portion: 1 slice bread + 1 tbsp peanut butter + 1 banana

steps: Toast bread; spread peanut butter.
Top with banana slices.
Choose no-sugar PB when possible (Food Pharmer-style label check).

nutritionNotes: 1 slice whole-grain bread ~70–80 kcal + 1 tbsp PB ~94 kcal + banana ~105 kcal (USDA components).

name: Light Mango Lassi
description: Diluted mango-curd drink for tasty carbs + some protein.
portion: 250ml light lassi (½ cup mango + 100g curd + water)

steps: Blend mango, curd, water.
Keep thinner than dessert lassi.
Sip 45–60 min pre-lift.

nutritionNotes: ½ cup mango (~80–90 kcal) + 100g curd + water dilution.

name: Orange–Spinach Smoothie
description: Vitamin C + greens blender fuel (pre or light post).

steps: Blend until smooth.
Drink fresh.
Add banana if you need more carbs.

nutritionNotes: 1 orange (~62 kcal, USDA) + 1 cup spinach (~7 kcal raw) blended in water.
